quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead when you:

options.text: Are following a small passenger vehicle.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: When another driver is tailgating you, add extra space in front of your vehicle. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a crash.

questions.question: If you find yourself in a skid:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake abruptly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes if your vehicle skids. Using brakes will make the skid worse.

questions.question: You are preparing to exit the interstate. When should you start reducing your speed?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to match the posted speed limit for the exit ramp.

questions.question: If dust or smoke is blowing across the road and you cannot see other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights anytime poor visibility prevents you from seeing other vehicles. Other drivers also need to see you.

questions.question: If you want to enter the freeway but do not see a gap in traffic, you should:

options.text: Maintain your speed and force the other drivers to create a gap.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap in traffic. Do not wait until the end of the ramp or you will not have enough space to speed up and merge safely.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange sign warns you that road work is coming. Pay attention to temporary traffic signs and equipment in work zones.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. Any trace of alcohol will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: At intersections with a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.
Yield the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if necessary. Give the right-of-way to any nearby traffic that could cause a conflict.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely on a two-lane road:

options.text: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
questions.explanation: If possible, change lanes to let the tailgater pass. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the other driver to pass you.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS will automatically pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street, where should you position your car?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
To the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, drive in the lane closest to the centerline. Turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Use hand-over-hand steering to turn into the first legal lane.

questions.question: If a work zone has no speed limit signs posted, what should you do?

options.text: Obey the normal speed limit.
Drive 15 mph slower than the posted speed limit.
Drive 15 mph faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the normal speed limit.
questions.explanation: Most work zones have signs showing reduced speed limits. If you do not see reduced speed limit signs in the work zone, follow the normal posted speed limit.

questions.question: On an interstate, how can you avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Watch for on-ramps ahead on interstate highways. When you can, move to the left lane to let vehicles enter from the on-ramps on your right.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What might the truck do?

options.text: Complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
Have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks have a bigger difference between these paths. This is why large trucks often need to swing wide when making a right turn.

questions.question: When a bicyclist makes a left turn, what can they do?

options.text: Use the left lane.
Cut through all lanes.
Wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Do not be surprised if you see a bicyclist using the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns you that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights. The light bounces back and shines into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Reduction in lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you never do when changing lanes?

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check for drivers passing you who may be entering your lane. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never change lanes in an intersection.

questions.question: If someone passes you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Maintain your speed and position.
Slow down to let the other driver safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let the other driver safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Passing areas are based on how far ahead drivers can see. Help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely and easily so everyone can avoid dangers ahead.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop completely. Let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are entering the highway on a short ramp with no acceleration lane. What should you do?

options.text: Go directly into the far-right lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the road shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you find an open space in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find an open space in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short ramp with no acceleration lane, speed up only after you spot a gap in traffic. Wait while stopped until a gap appears.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot possible dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for dangers. Do not stare only at the road right in front of you. Scan ahead and watch for vehicles around you.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side of the road means you can cross it to pass. You may pass when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: You park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: On a road with no curb, turn your wheels so the car rolls away from the center if brakes fail. Turn right when parked uphill.
